Name: FarmQueue
Author: MLD210
Description:
[left]Farm Queue
Draw a rectangle. Your farmer does the rest.
[heading]What is this?[/heading]
Farm Queue lets you select an area of your farm by dragging a rectangle, and then your farmer automatically walks over and completes every job inside it with what you are holding.
No more clicking tile by tile. No more walking back and forth to refill your watering can. No more forgetting which corner of the field you already finished.
Hold an item, hold LeftControl, drag a box, let go. That's it.
It is not only tools. A box can also mean [i]"pet, milk and shear everything in here"[/i], [i]"clear this whole messy corner — switching tools as you go"[/i], or [i]"collect every finished machine and refill it with what I'm holding"[/i].
[b]Inspired by ActionQueue Reborn[/b]
This mod is directly inspired by ActionQueue Reborn for Don't Starve Together.
In DST, ActionQueue Reborn lets you queue up a chain of actions and then watch your character execute them one by one — a small quality-of-life idea that completely changes how the game feels to play. Stardew Valley has a very similar problem: farming is repetitive, and most of the friction is not in deciding what to do, but in physically performing the same click hundreds of times.
Farm Queue brings that same idea to Stardew Valley. Instead of queueing a list of individual actions, you simply paint the area you want worked, and the queue works out the rest — which tile to visit first, how much to charge the hoe, when to walk around an obstacle, and how to get to a water source without being told.
All credit for the original concept goes to the ActionQueue Reborn author. This is a Stardew Valley interpretation of that idea.
[heading]How it works[/heading]
[list=1]
[*]Equip the tool or item you want to use.[/*]
[/list][list=1]
[*]Hold [b]LeftControl[/b] and drag with the [b]left mouse button[/b] to paint a rectangle over the ground. Both the modifier key and the selection button can be rebound in the config menu.[/*]
[/list][list=1]
[*]Tiles are highlighted as you drag:
[list]
[*][b]Green[/b] — this tile has a job your held item can do.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Red[/b] — nothing to do here with this item (already finished, wrong tool, blocked, out of sprinkler range, etc.).[/*]
[/list][/*]
[/list][list=1]
[*]Release the mouse button. The queue starts.[/*]
[/list]Your farmer then walks to each valid tile and performs the action. Charged tools automatically use the widest charge level that stays inside the area you painted — the mod will never till outside your rectangle.
Once the run starts, the queued tiles are drawn as a green grid on the ground (or the queued animal / tree / machine glows), and a small exclamation bubble marks whatever is next. Both can be switched off.
[heading]One box, several tools[/heading]
Box a messy corner while holding a [b]scythe, axe or pickaxe[/b] and the queue does not do "all the weeds, then all the twigs, then all the stones" — it works the box as a single route and swaps tools per tile: weeds under your feet go to the scythe, the nearest twig switches to the axe, the next stone switches to the pickaxe.
The tool you were holding when you closed the box is put back when the run ends or is interrupted. Tools you don't actually carry are treated as absent, and tiles only they could handle are not marked green while you drag.
[heading]Animals[/heading]
Box your coop or barn with the right thing in hand and the same queue handles the animals:
[table][tr][td]Holding[/td]
[td]What is queued[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Nothing, or any non-tool item[/td]
[td]Pet every animal that hasn't been petted today[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Milk Pail[/td]
[td]Milk every ready animal[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Shears[/td]
[td]Shear every ready animal[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Scythe[/td]
[td]Collect produce and pick up dropped items inside the box[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]Your farmer opens fence gates on the way when that is the only way in. Animals that are asleep, or that have nothing to give today, are reported in the summary instead of being silently skipped — and if your bag is full, the run stops and tells you rather than dropping the produce on the ground.
[heading]Machines: collect and refill in one pass[/heading]
Hold a machine input (fruit, ore, seed, …) and box a wall of kegs, jars or furnaces: every [b]finished[/b] machine is harvested first and then refilled with what you are holding, in the same visit. Machines that are still processing are left alone.
Recipes that consume several items per load (coffee beans into a keg, for example) work too. If a machine's output won't fit in your bag, it is skipped for this run and counted in the summary.
[heading]Garden pots[/heading]
Garden pots are treated as normal targets: sowing, harvesting and machine loading all work on a pot field, and the farmer reaches them from the walkway instead of trying to stand on the pot.
[heading]Stopping and pausing[/heading]
Press any movement key (WASD / arrow keys) at any time to stop the queue. Opening a menu, switching tools, or alt-tabbing also pauses it safely.
The queue also stops itself and says why, when:
[list]
[*]it is [b]2:00 AM[/b] (so you don't pass out mid-row),[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]your [b]stamina[/b] drops below the configured floor (15 by default, the vanilla "too tired" threshold),[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]your [b]bag is full[/b] and the next job needs room,[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]you run [b]out of seeds / fertilizer / saplings / sprinklers / the item itself[/b].[/*]
[/list][heading]What each tool can do[/heading]
[table][tr][td]Held item[/td]
[td]Queued actions[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Hoe[/td]
[td]Till soil, clear weeds, dig artifact spots and seed spots[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Watering Can[/td]
[td]Water crops. Walks to a water source and refills automatically when empty[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Seeds[/td]
[td]Sow on tilled soil, including trellis crops like hops and grapes[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Fertilizer[/td]
[td]Apply to tilled soil[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Sapling[/td]
[td]Plant fruit trees and other saplings[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Scythe[/td]
[td]Cut grass (normal and blue), clear weeds, harvest scythe-able crops, harvest moss off trees, collect machine output and animal produce, pick up forage[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Pickaxe[/td]
[td]Break stones, ore nodes, geodes and boulders, clear weeds, remove flooring and paths, pick up placed objects and fences, flatten unwanted tilled soil[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Axe[/td]
[td]Chop trees, stumps, logs and twigs, clear weeds, remove fruit trees, harvest giant crops[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Sprinkler[/td]
[td]Place sprinklers on a planned grid[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Machine input[/td]
[td]Walk to machines and load them (kegs, furnaces, preserves jars, …), harvesting finished ones first[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Milk Pail / Shears[/td]
[td]Milk / shear animals inside the box[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Nothing[/td]
[td]Pet animals inside the box[/td]
[/tr]
[tr][td]Other placeable objects[/td]
[td]Place them on the ground[/td]
[/tr]
[/table][heading]Features[/heading]
[list]
[*][b]Charge matching[/b] — charged tools pick the largest charge that does not spill outside your selection. No accidental extra tilling.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Automatic refill[/b] — the watering can walks to the nearest water source and refills without being asked, then resumes exactly where it left off.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Path-aware ordering[/b] — the route is planned by real walking distance through corridors, not straight lines. Keg spirals, greenhouse aisles and maze-like layouts are worked in the order you would walk them, without cutting through walls.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Sprinkler-aware filtering[/b] — optionally restrict tilling or sowing to only the tiles your sprinklers actually cover.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Smart placement order[/b] — for seeds and solid objects, the mod plans placements so your farmer does not trap themselves between solid objects, and opens a gap at the end of each row to walk through.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Obstacle handling[/b] — slimes, rock crabs and farm animals that physically block the way are sidestepped like a player would; a tile that cannot be reached is retried at the end instead of stalling.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Per-tool toggles[/b] — decide exactly which jobs the queue is allowed to do with each tool.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Idle-only machine loading[/b] — never touches a machine that is still processing or already finished.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]On-screen feedback[/b] — "Selected 12 x 8 = 96 tiles (72 workable / 24 blocked)" while dragging, "Tilling: 40 left" while working, plus exclamation bubbles over whatever is next.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Opens your backpack when a run finishes on its own[/b] — in single player that pauses time, so nothing runs away while you are away.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Layout presets[/b] — sprinkler grid layouts, including a dedicated trellis-crop layout with configurable spacing.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Charge animation control[/b] — skip the wind-up animation entirely, or speed it up; range and stamina cost are unaffected.[/*]
[/list][heading]Installation[/heading]
[list=1]
[*]Install [url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI 4.0.0 or newer[/url].[/*]
[/list][list=1]
[*]Download this mod and unzip it into your
[code]Stardew Valley/Mods[/code]folder.[/*]
[/list][list=1]
[*]Launch the game through SMAPI.[/*]
[/list]Your Mods folder should then look like this:
[heading]Configuration[/heading]
Open Generic Mod Config Menu (GMCM) and click the cog next to Farm Queue. Every behavior can be switched on or off per tool, so you can keep the queue strictly to the jobs you actually want automated.
The menu is organised into sections:
[list]
[*][b]General[/b] — modifier key, selection button, charge animation, stamina floor, status text, task bubbles, open backpack on finish, auto-switch tools for debris[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Hoe[/b] — what counts as a job, sprinkler-range-only tilling[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Watering Can[/b] — water only planted crops, auto-refill behavior[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Seeds[/b] — sprinkler-range-only sowing[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Scythe[/b] — crops, flowers, forage, moss, blue grass, normal grass, dead crops, weeds, machine output[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Pickaxe[/b] — stones, boulders, flooring, placed objects, fences, flattening[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Axe[/b] — trees, stumps, twigs, weeds, fruit trees, giant crops[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Machine Loading[/b] — idle machines only[/*]
[/list][list]
[*][b]Layout[/b] — sprinkler grid layout and spacing, sapling spacing[/*]
[/list]All menu labels, on-screen status text and action names follow your game language automatically. English and Chinese are built in; other languages fall back to English.
[heading]Translations[/heading]
[list]
[*]English[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]简体中文 (Simplified Chinese)[/*]
[/list]The mod follows your game language automatically. English and Simplified Chinese are included; other languages fall back to English. To add a language, drop a new file into the
[code]i18n[/code]folder.
[heading]Requirements[/heading]
[list]
[*]SMAPI 4.0.0 or newer[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Stardew Valley 1.6+[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Generic Mod Config Menu — optional, strongly recommended[/*]
[/list][heading]Compatibility[/heading]
Works alongside most SMAPI mods. It operates through the same hooks the game itself uses (tool usage, item placement, machine loading, animal interaction), so mods that change those systems should behave normally. Scythe behaviour adapts to mods such as HarvestWithScythe, and trellis crops made passable by mods are walked through rather than around.
If you find a conflict, please report it with your SMAPI log — it is the fastest way to diagnose compatibility issues.
[heading]Feedback[/heading]
Bug reports and suggestions are very welcome. If something goes wrong, please include:
[list]
[*]What you were doing (which tool, which area)[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Your SMAPI log[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]A description of what you expected vs. what happened[/*]
[/list][heading]Credits[/heading]
Author: MLD[/left]
